board: Louisiana State Board of Certified Public Accountants

cycle.note: Louisiana CPE runs by calendar year, completed by December 31 and reported online by January 31: at least 20 hours a year and 80 over the rolling two calendar years, plus a Board-approved ethics course in even-numbered years. No carryover; nano-learning doesn't count.

requirements.label: Two-year total
requirements.note: Last year plus this year must reach 80 hours (LAC 46:XIX.1301). The year you were licensed counts as 20.

requirements.label: Minimum each year
requirements.note: At least 20 hours every calendar year.

requirements.label: Accounting & auditing
requirements.note: If you take part in attest engagements this year (audits, reviews, compilations, agreed-upon procedures): at least 8 hours of accounting and auditing.

requirements.label: Personal development
requirements.note: Maximum, not a target. Personal development over 20 hours in a calendar year is disallowed.

requirements.label: Nano-learning
requirements.note: Nano-learning isn't accepted for CPE credit in Louisiana (Board CPE page).

requirements.label: Louisiana ethics
requirements.note: In even-numbered years, a Board-approved Louisiana ethics course (3 hours in 2026). General ethics doesn't count. We count courses with "Louisiana" and "ethics" in the title.

newLicensee.note: No CPE is due in the calendar year you were licensed; it starts the next full calendar year.

practiceOptions.label: Attest engagements (audits, reviews, compilations, agreed-upon procedures)

licenseDateHint: Louisiana certificates renew every year by December 31. CPE is tracked by calendar year.
issueDateHint: If you were licensed this year, no CPE is due until next year.
limitsNotTracked: Published materials: max 10 hours a year; teaching/speaking (with preparation): max 20; credentialing exams: max 20.
Self-study must be interactive (most NASBA QAS courses are).
Personal development and nano-learning over the limit come off this year's hours; earlier years' excess isn't re-checked.
Credit is in 50-minute hours, rounded down to the nearest half hour.
Louisiana ethics isn't needed if you mainly practice in another state that has its own ethics requirement and hold an active license there.
Non-residents can instead meet their principal-place-of-business state's CPE rules (signed statement at renewal).
recordRetention: Keep CPE documentation (and course materials showing content and instructors) for five full calendar years after each program.
toVerify: Louisiana ethics hours in future even years (3 in 2026; earlier years were 2).
Licensure year counted as 20 toward the two-year 80 (sources: '60 the following year').
